pinned_confirmations.note: both rounds act on a group Roadmap 8.3's helper incepted here. Its identifier differs from that item's fixture because the key states are different: a group rotation only works if the members' key states chain, so the next digests here are derived from the member's own salt where `mockGetAID` invents them.

a_rotation_is_announced_on_the_interacti.declaration: in `multisig.test.ts` only the initiator sends `/multisig/rot`; both joining members send the same `rot` embed under `/multisig/ixn`, while both peers wait on `/multisig/rot`
a_rotation_is_announced_on_the_interacti.note: the route says interaction and the embed carries a rotation, so a member that trusts the route reads the wrong message and one that waits on the rotation route never sees the join at all. Nothing upstream compares the two, because nothing upstream looks inside the embed.
a_rotation_is_announced_on_the_interacti.rust_decision: the route decides the embed. Roadmap 8.1's classifier refuses a message whose embed slot is not the one its route names, so this pair cannot be built here — `propose_rotation` and `accept_rotation` both send `/multisig/rot`.

a_joining_member_never_reads_the_rotatio.declaration: `multisig.test.ts` calls `rotate` again with its own `states`/`rstates` and signs whatever that produces; `multisig-join.test.ts` rebuilds the proposed `Serder` and signs that

divergent.rebuilt_from: a rotation set of the same size whose next digests differ from the proposal's

a_joining_member_never_reads_the_rotatio.note: the two styles agree only while the members' key states do. Driven both ways: with the same states the digests match, and with one rotation member where the proposal named two the rebuilding member signs a different event — no error, no comparison, and the signature it contributes is over something nobody proposed. This is Roadmap 8.3's witness threshold in a second place.
a_joining_member_never_reads_the_rotatio.rust_decision: a joining member checks. `accept_rotation` rebuilds as the reference does and then compares what it built with the digest the proposal carries, refusing to sign a different event. A digest comparison rather than a byte one, because a decoded record cannot reproduce the bytes it arrived as — but an event's SAID is a digest over the event, so two events with one SAID are one event.

an_interaction_relays_the_data_it_read.declaration: `multisig.test.ts` reads `exn.e.ixn.a` and passes it straight back into `interact`, where `delegateMultisig` reads `ixn.a[0]`
an_interaction_relays_the_data_it_read.note: this is the half the reference gets right: the joining member anchors the same seal the initiator did, because `createInteract` wraps a non-array and leaves an array alone. The two readers disagree about the shape — one takes the array, the other its first element — but both reach the same seal.
an_interaction_relays_the_data_it_read.rust_decision: reproduced. The anchors are read from the embedded event and passed through unchanged.
